- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.4) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if true price drops sharply after a spike, model often holds high values for 2–3 days beyond the peak.
- Reduce forecast magnitude when sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.3) — model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts.
- Apply downward bias correction for 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6) — model overweights recent highs.
- Avoid extrapolating upward from recent highs if sentiment is declining — model often ignores sentiment decay.
- For 10+ day horizons, reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment is below 0.5 — model tends to overproject recovery.
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.8, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — model often mirrors sentiment peaks without adjusting for underlying price momentum.
